🚨 SECURITY RESEARCHER ALLEGES "TEDDY KEYBOARD" APP EXPOSED USER PHOTOS AND USED DECEPTIVE CARRIER BILLING

A security researcher using the handle u/HTML_H4CKER has published findings alleging serious privacy and billing issues involving the "Teddy Keyboard" Android application.

According to the researcher's analysis, the application's backend contained functionality for uploading user photos and profile pictures, while directories containing what appeared to be user images were reportedly accessible on the server.

The researcher shared screenshots of backend source code and the exposed image repository as supporting evidence.

Key findings alleged by the researcher:

* Backend scripts named upload_photos.php and upload_profile_pic.php handled image uploads
* Numerous apparent user photos were discovered in server directories
* The researcher says the application's privacy policy did not disclose this storage behavior
* Screenshots show backend code referencing profile image storage and user records
* A database backup containing a large number of user entries was reportedly accessible
* The exposed photo directories and upload paths were later taken offline

The researcher also alleges a separate billing issue.

According to the report, users logging into Teddy Keyboard could be enrolled in a 300 LKR subscription through an Ideamart carrier-billing service.

The researcher claims the subscription disclosure was displayed in very small text and that the OTP users entered during login could also authorize the premium subscription.

Uninstalling the application would reportedly NOT automatically cancel the carrier subscription.

⚠️ IMPORTANT:

These findings currently represent allegations and technical evidence published by an independent researcher.

We have not seen an official response from Teddy Keyboard, Google, Ideamart or the relevant authorities confirming the full scope of the claims.

The screenshots demonstrate backend functionality and apparent exposed data, but by themselves do not establish exactly how many users were affected or under what circumstances every photograph was uploaded.

⚠️ Analyst Note:

If independently confirmed, there are two separate security concerns here.

The first is privacy: applications collecting or storing personal media need clear consent, appropriate disclosure and strong access controls.

The second is deceptive billing. When authentication and subscription authorization are combined into a user experience that does not clearly communicate the financial transaction, users may not understand what they are consenting to.

This case is another reminder that mobile-app risk extends far beyond malware.

Backend security, privacy practices, third-party billing integrations and consent mechanisms can be just as important as the application installed on the device.
